first.text:
Here's what the amend looks like before anything is recorded. Three things change, two things need your call.

**1. Pull-up dose.** The negatives and the band pull-ups now count toward the strict pull-up's weekly figure, so the target can be a real number instead of a placeholder, and the note explaining the placeholder is gone. As the week stands, Wednesday delivers 3 hard sets of negatives and 4 of band pull-ups, and Friday adds the strict single: 8 hard sets a week. My recommendation is a target of **8**. It sits inside the 5–15 range, it matches what the week already delivers, and it won't nag you every week about a shortfall you'd have to add sets to close. I've pencilled 10 for now as the "raise it" option; 10 would mean one more set of negatives and one more band set on Wednesday, and Wednesday has the time for it (39 minutes of 75). Tell me 8 or 10 and I'll set it before adopting.

**2. Swings.** The kettlebell swing finisher leaves Monday's pressing session and becomes its own conditioning session beside it: 12 minutes, one set of 12 swings at the top of each minute at 40 lb, effort about 7 of 10. When a session comes in at or under that effort, the clock grows by 2 minutes up to 16, then the reps climb toward 15. Monday's lifting drops to an estimated 47 minutes of its 75 without the swings. It's optional, so a skipped swing session never counts against your adherence. Once adopted, a logged swing session will be read as conditioning work rather than lifting sets, so the swings stop padding your hard-set count; I'll confirm that on the first one you log. Your logged workout from the 2nd stays exactly as it is.

**3. Circuit.** Unchanged, and under the new rules a standing session sits outside the same-day stacking check in both directions, so the weekly note you had to add about it won't be asked for again. The one on this week's plan is already there and harmless; it simply won't come back next week.

**The warnings as they stand:**

- *New, and it needs your call:* the deadlift's weekly target of 4 hard sets is under the 5-set floor. This was always true; the pull-up placeholder was masking it. Two honest options: raise it to 5 (one more working set on Sunday; Sunday is at 65 of 90 minutes) or keep 4 with a reason, which would be that the Tuesday legs session sometimes includes deadlifts the trainer programmes and you're in maintenance. I lean toward 5, since the deadlift is the lift furthest from its target.
- *Kept, already explained:* the strict single on Friday is a weekly measure, not a progression, while your max is 1. The negatives and band work do the building.
- *Not from this change:* Monday's routine in Hevy has drifted from the week's plan (reps on the last three sets of the press and the row's weights). It clears itself on the next push; nothing to do now.

No new or filled defaults; the block continues; rotation stays where it is. I won't push anything to Hevy until you say the kit tables are ready.

So: pull-up target 8 or 10, deadlift target 5 or keep 4 with that reason, and then your yes to adopt.
